page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a 1.0 thread-per-core topology, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. It features 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark results position the ecs.hfg6.8xlarge consistently in the middle 50% average tier across all tested categories. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1436.68 and a multi-core score of 30666.35. Memory performance tests show a cached read-only small block bandwidth of 1705.41 GB/sec, which drops to 109.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 48.22 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the server processed 28.91 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved a static web serving throughput of 21.45 GB/sec. Software compilation via Clang scored 23704.0 on Geekbench, while LLM inference speeds reached 12.4 tokens per second for text generation on a medium 7B model.

From a resource density perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offer a balanced hardware profile for workloads requiring consistent compute power without the overhead of shared-core virtualization. However, the complete absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on external network storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy tasks. Given these characteristics, the instance is suited for multi-threaded CPU tasks, software compilation, static web serving, and database operations that fit within its 128.0 GB memory capacity.
